transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess I'm just having some trouble at work. I work at a dry cleaners, and... I just can't seem to keep things in order anymore. 

It's just... the tickets and receipts, the customer jobs, workshop notes... they all just end up piled together. And then I look at it and I just... I don't know what to handle first. So... that's why I'm here.
Have you struggled with staying organized and keeping track of tasks like this for as long as you can remember, even back in school, or is this something that's really only started recently?

Um... I suppose it's not really new. 

Even back in grade school... my teachers used to tell my mother I was bright, but just... scattered. I guess I was always talking out of turn. And losing my papers. They always had to remind me to actually finish my work... so, yeah. It's always been like this.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still for long periods, like during meetings or meals?

I guess... yeah. I don't really like sitting for that long. 

Like, if I have to go to a church committee meeting, or... those fabric-care trainings we do for work. I usually find some reason to get up. Just to get water, or... check on some papers or something. I just notice I'm up doing that when everybody else is just sitting still.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out answers before a question is finished, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Um... I suppose so, yes. I do that. 

Like with my daughter, or... a customer at the counter. Or the trainer at work. I just... I jump in with an answer before they're even finished asking. And then... well, sometimes I find out I answered the wrong thing. Because I didn't wait. So... yeah.
Would you say these struggles with organization, restlessness, and interrupting cause real problems for you not just at work, but also at home or in your relationships with family?

I suppose so. Yes. 

At the shop, it's... well, things get mixed up. Some orders go out late, or the billing gets confused. It causes some... tense moments, I guess. With the other girls working there, and the customers. 

And at home... well, at church, I used to help plan things. But I stepped back from leading. People were just... they were getting frustrated with me. So I stopped.

Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, can you recall specific examples—like report cards or things teachers or parents said—that show these attention or restlessness issues were already noticeable that early?

Um... well, I guess so. Yes. 

My mother... she kept some of my old report cards from grade school. The teachers always wrote the same sort of things. They said I was bright, but... scattered. 

I was always talking out of turn. Or I'd lose my assignments. They always had to remind me to just... finish what I was doing. So, yes. It was like that back then, too.
